Subject: BrightLane: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding & surge readiness

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're ready to move from discovery to provisioning for the Dedicated GPU pool. High level asks from our side:

- Guaranteed baseline of 80 concurrent vCPU-like dedicated endpoints (model: 13B family) across us-west-2 and us-east-1.
- Autoscale policy that supports burst up to 2.5x baseline with <30s cold-start target.
- Warmup / prefetch plan to avoid initial latency spikes, especially for long-context inference.
- Clear canary schedule and rollback criteria for traffic ramp.

Can you confirm the recommended pool topology, burst policy, and an initial runbook for the warmup phase? Procurement is ready to sign once we have a brief SLA addendum and the PO (see attached stub).

Attachments: BrightLane_PO_453.pdf (stub)

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, full plan attached below.

- Topology: two regional pools (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 active-standby with cross-region spillover). Each pool will be provisioned with a baseline node count sized to meet 80 concurrent steady-state requests given your 13B profile; estimated baseline: 12 g4/8-type nodes per region (we'll run a short perf sim before finalizing).
- Burst policy: configured autoscale up to 250% of baseline with burst credit throttles and graceful shedding (traffic routed to compatible quantized model variant when <30s cold-start cannot be met).
- Warmup: automated prefix cache prefill + a 45-minute staggered synthetic traffic ramp that pins KV caches and primes sharded attention kernels.
- Canary: 4-phase canary (0.5% / 5% / 25% / 100%) with automated regression checks on latency P95, error-rate, and quality delta on a short evaluation prompt set. Rollback triggers: >15% P95 increase, >1.5% error rise, or any quality delta > threshold.

I've attached a short runbook (surge-warmup-runbook.xlsx) with timeline options and an SLA addendum template for procurement. Next concrete steps I propose:

1) Karthik and I run a perf sim (30–60m) Tues morning to validate baseline node counts.
2) Ops (Soojin) will draft the canary cadence and set up the synthetic warmup harness.
3) Emily/Procurement to confirm PO + preferred SLA edits by EOD Monday.

I'll schedule the perf sim and ping the team with calendar invites.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Emily/Jasmine — quick technical checklist ahead of perf sim and provisioning. Notes below are operational items we need confirmed from BrightLane ops:

- Peak sequence length distribution (we need 90th/99th percentile token lengths).
- Average tokens per request and expected concurrency distribution over a 24h period.
- Any preference for quantized model variants (int8 vs bf16 mixed precision) — we recommend int8 for cost but bf16 for tight-latency quality-sensitive routes.
- KV cache TTL expectations and whether cross-request reuse is expected between sessions (affects cache sizing).
- IP allowlist for dedicated control-plane access (CI/CD deploy hooks).

Operational items from our side:
- We'll enable prefix caching and a short-lived pre-warm layer that persists for 2h after heavy bursts.
- Autoscale policy will include a burst-smoothing window (90s) to avoid oscillation.
- We will ship a small tracer token in canary to capture tail-latency and KV hit-rate.

If you can reply with the distribution numbers and a contact for procurement confirmation, I'll lock the perf sim parameters.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in the ops checklist and canary run cadence I propose. Summary:

- Canary timeline (fast option): Day 0 (provision, smoke test), Day 1 (0.5% -> 5% with warmup harness), Day 2 (25%), Day 3 (100% if green). Each step has a minimum 2-hour observation window; automated monitors will evaluate P95 latency, error-rate, and eval-set quality.
- Fallback policy: immediate fallback to hosted-compatible quantized shard in same region if P95 > target for two consecutive windows. Cross-region spillover only used after fallback fails.
- Warmup details: 45m synthetic ramp per region with KV pinning, followed by traffic seeding from a small set of production-like sessions. We'll need an allowlist IP range for our synthetic agents.

I'll prepare a short runbook page that operations can follow; Jasmine, want me to attach the runbook to the DocuSign so procurement can see it?

-Soojin

Thanks everyone — this looks good and actionable. Answers below:

- Sequence lengths: 90th = 768 tokens, 99th = 2048 tokens. Avg tokens/request ~ 120. Concurrency spikes mostly during business hours (12:00–16:00 PT).
- We prefer int8 for the bulk of traffic; we'll reserve bf16 routes for our latency-sensitive endpoints (~10% of traffic).
- KV reuse: moderate cross-request reuse expected for sessionized users; TTL target 30m.
- Allowlist range for synthetic agents and control-plane hooks: 198.51.100.0/24

Procurement will send the signed PO this morning (BrightLane_PO_453.pdf attached). We have one small SLA ask: a 15-minute escalation hotline option during the D0–D3 canary window. Is that feasible?

If you can confirm the perf sim slot for Tues 08:30 PT, we will be on the call.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily

Emily Park
